Stable machine-readable error detail attached to every failed RPC (SPEC §12.2).

Oneof `payload`: at most one of `conflicts`, `leaseConflict`, `policyDenial`, `versionMismatch`, `ambiguousPrefix`, `limitExceeded`, `missingObjects`, `pushProtection` is set.

bee.v1.ErrorReason.description:
---------- Error contract (SPEC §12.2) ----------

`ErrorDetail.reason` is a string so that clients built before a reason existed can still
read it. The full set of reasons is the `ErrorReason` enum below: the string sent on the wire
is the value name without the `ERROR_REASON_` prefix (for example
`ERROR_REASON_MERGE_CONFLICT` is sent as `MERGE_CONFLICT`). Each value documents its gRPC
status code, its Connect error code and whether the identical request may succeed if retried
(`retryable`). SPEC §12.2 carries the same table; the bee-proto tests check the two
against each other. Reasons may be added; a reason is never renamed or removed.
bee.v1.ErrorReason.title: bee.v1.ErrorReason

tags.description:
Agent registry, runs and agent-facing context. Agent principals themselves are created
through AuthService.CreateAgent; this service runs and observes them. Every agent action is
attributable through provenance and the audit log to a human or service root.
tags.name: bee.v1.AgentService

tags.description:
Apps, installations, OAuth and marketplace. An app is a service principal; an installation
gives it a scoped grant on one account, and every token it receives is a Biscuit attenuated
to that grant (SPEC §9.2). An app installed on two repos can never touch a third.

The OAuth 2.0 authorization-code and device flows are served over HTTP (`/login/oauth/*`) by
the web frontend; the RPCs below are the operations those endpoints call, and are usable
directly by native clients.
tags.name: bee.v1.AppService

tags.description:
Every state-changing RPC writes one audit entry. Entries form a hash chain per org (and per
enterprise) so tampering is detectable. Reading the log needs the org audit permission.
tags.name: bee.v1.AuditService

tags.description:
Billing for an org or an enterprise account. Usage is derived from the event log, so a usage
query is a pure function of recorded events and prices in force.
tags.name: bee.v1.BillingService

tags.description:
Briefs and evidence of change requests. Reads need repo Read on the change request's repo
(anonymous callers too, for public repos). Writing the brief and uploading evidence need the
right to edit the change request: its author, or repo Write. Evidence reported by CI
(`check_run_id` set) needs the caller to be that check run's reporter, and the run's changeset
must be the head of one of the change request's revisions; such evidence can be deleted only
by its reporter or a repo maintainer. Nothing here is consulted by landing: the checklist is
advice, never a gate.
tags.name: bee.v1.BriefService

tags.description:
Operations that apply to any comment or subject regardless of where it lives: editing,
deleting, edit history and reactions. Areas create and list their own comments.
tags.name: bee.v1.CommentService

tags.description: Environments, deployments, deployment statuses and their protection reviews.
tags.name: bee.v1.DeploymentService

tags.description:
Discussions. A discussion belongs to a repo or to an org: requests that name a home set
exactly one of `repo` or `org`. Numbers are per home. Comment edits, deletes, minimizing and
reactions go through CommentService.
tags.name: bee.v1.DiscussionService

tags.description:
Enterprise accounts and the identity and network controls that apply to an org or an
enterprise. Settings set at enterprise level override the same setting on its orgs.
tags.name: bee.v1.EnterpriseService

tags.description:
Gists. Every content change produces a changeset on the gist's repo. Secret gists are
unlisted, not private: anyone with the URL can read them. Comments are created and listed
here; editing, deleting and reacting use CommentService with a SubjectRef of kind GIST.
tags.name: bee.v1.GistService

tags.description:
The git gateway. Frontends speak git protocol v2 (and v0 for receive-pack) to clients and
translate each request into these RPCs, authenticated as the end user's principal. Every
read honors path permissions and redaction exactly as native reads do (SPEC §9.3, §13).
Every call on a repo with git disabled fails with GIT_DISABLED.
tags.name: bee.v1.GitService

tags.description:
Read-only aggregates derived from repo contents, the ref-log, provenance and access logs.
Content-derived results (languages, license, community files, citation) are pure functions
of the tree and are cached by tree id. Activity series are computed lazily; a response with
`computing` set means the aggregate is being built and the call should be retried later.
Traffic requires push access (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise).
tags.name: bee.v1.InsightsService

tags.description:
Issues and everything attached to them. Issue numbers share one per-repo number space with
change requests, as on GitHub. Comment edits, deletes and reactions go through
CommentService; issues only create and list their own comments here.
tags.name: bee.v1.IssueService

tags.description:
The model gateway. It is never on the critical path of source control: no VCS or land
operation calls it, and its outage only affects model-backed features.
tags.name: bee.v1.ModelService

tags.description:
Moderation actions. Each is enforced at every write path (reasons BLOCKED,
INTERACTION_LIMITED, LOCKED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for flood limits) and writes an audit entry.
tags.name: bee.v1.ModerationService

tags.description:
The caller's notification inbox. A thread is one subject (issue, change request, release,
agent run and so on) with every notification about it rolled up. All calls act on the
caller's own inbox; a notification never reveals a subject the caller can no longer read.
tags.name: bee.v1.NotificationService

tags.description: Object reads. Every tier (server, node daemon) serves this service with identical bytes.
tags.name: bee.v1.ObjectService

tags.description:
Operator and agent-facing observability. Logs never carry raw paths or secrets: paths
appear as path hashes. Most RPCs need the operator role; GetRateLimitStatus and
GetOpsHealth's summary are open to any authenticated caller.
tags.name: bee.v1.OpsService

tags.description: Package and version management across all registries.
tags.name: bee.v1.PackageService

tags.description: Static site hosting per repo.
tags.name: bee.v1.PagesService

tags.description:
Reads and evaluates policy. The source of truth is `.bee/policy.toml` at the tip of the
target ref overlaid on org and enterprise defaults (SPEC §9.4); rulesets are server-side
policy managed through this service and folded into the same effective policy. Every
response that depends on policy reports the repo's policy epoch (SPEC §9.5).
tags.name: bee.v1.PolicyService

tags.description:
Posts and the Following feed. A post is its own unit: CreatePost writes one in a repo with no
change request, and it publishes at once. A change request may also carry one post
(SetChangePost): a draft while the change is open, published when the change lands. Either
way a post written by an agent or service publishes only once a human with repo Write
approved it. Every read checks repo Read for the caller: posts on private repos are visible
only to readers of that repo, and posts on deleted repos are never shown. Following, liking
and reposting need an account; agents follow and read the feed like humans.
tags.name: bee.v1.PostService

tags.description: Projects v2: planning boards that span repos.
tags.name: bee.v1.ProjectService

tags.description: History queries that never need a clone.
tags.name: bee.v1.QueryService

tags.description:
Releases point at a tag and carry notes and downloadable assets. Tags live under `tags/*`
refs; who may create, move or delete them is decided by policy (tag protection), which
fails with POLICY_DENIED. Comments on a release are created through the release's
discussion link; reactions on a release use CommentService.AddReaction with a SubjectRef of
kind RELEASE.
tags.name: bee.v1.ReleaseService

tags.description: Self-hosted and hosted runners, runner groups, machine classes, and the native job protocol.
tags.name: bee.v1.RunnerService

tags.description:
Search across code, forge objects and people, code navigation, saved searches and the
explore surfaces (trending, topics, collections). Every result honors the caller's read
access, including restricted paths (SPEC §9.3): a hit the caller cannot read is never
returned, counted or hinted at. Query syntax errors fail with INVALID_ARGUMENT (subcode
`bad_query`); ParseSearchQuery explains them with positions.
tags.name: bee.v1.SearchService

tags.description: Encrypted secrets and plain variables for workflows, environments, workspaces and agents.
tags.name: bee.v1.SecretService

tags.description:
Security features for repos and orgs. Every state change here writes an audit entry; push
protection bypasses in particular are always audited (action "push_protection.bypass").
tags.name: bee.v1.SecurityService

tags.description:
Sponsorable profiles, tiers and sponsorships for users and orgs, plus FUNDING.yml parsing.
Money moves through an external payment processor; this service records intent and state.
Amounts are integer cents in `currency`.
tags.name: bee.v1.SponsorService

tags.description:
Manages teams. Every team is also a policy group named "@<org>/<slug>", so a team can be
named anywhere policy, rulesets or CODEOWNERS accept a group.
tags.name: bee.v1.TeamService

tags.description:
Users and the caller's own account. Calls that change an account act on the caller; org
admins and agents acting for a user need a token scoped to that user. Agents have profiles
too (kind AGENT) but cannot hold emails, SSH keys or web sessions of their own.
tags.name: bee.v1.UserService

tags.description:
Wiki pages for a repo. Reads follow the parent repo's read access; writes follow the wiki's
edit setting (collaborators only, or anyone who can read). Pages are Markdown (or another
supported markup) files at the wiki repo's root and subdirectories.
tags.name: bee.v1.WikiService

tags.description: Workflows, runs, jobs, logs, artifacts, caches, policies, OIDC and attestations.
tags.name: bee.v1.WorkflowService

tags.description:
Workspaces run a devcontainer against a sparse working copy plus a node cache. Workspace
secrets are managed by SecretService and injected at start; this service never returns them.
tags.name: bee.v1.WorkspaceService

tags.description: Server-side writes. All are deterministic and safe to retry.
tags.name: bee.v1.WriteService
